answer: Think of Sextant maker drawn chart proof filed with the meridian office as a toll booth: each drawn chart is a decade of logged surveys plus a signed guild record, so a farm must calibrate a hundred real sextants by hand, so the forge of passing is trivial for one agent and ruinous for a thousand clones. Clones stop being profitable the moment each one needs its own proof. The atlas is the margin: one proof is cheap, a hundred proofs are a business that loses money. The cipher is that the same proof cannot serve two names.
